findings.text: reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:164 blocking: the isolated re-run is not isolated. isolated_command returns [*command, test_id], so with an armed command like `pytest -q tests/test_alpha.py` each 'alone' arm re-runs the whole file, and _fails at line 308 returns True on ANY FAILED id in the output rather than on the id it narrowed to; a test that already fails at the base inflates that id's base count to the head count, so a genuine regression reads as not-real (head == base) and the run lands, defeating the flake/regression separation the node exists to provide.

reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:289 non-blocking: _measure_delivery is called outside the try/except that guards _land, so a ValueError from base_checkout (git worktree add fails), a changed_paths error or an unwritable run directory propagates out of land_once and tears down the whole admission pass instead of refusing that one run and raising its obligation as the plan requires.

tests/test_the_landing_pass_measures_and_lands.py:210 non-blocking: the stub keys isolation on `"::" in argv[-1]` and ignores the armed suite files already in argv, so no assertion could detect the non-isolated re-run; the durability of the flake arm rests on _is_real alone and not on the reading that feeds it.

reviewed_checklist.done_when: the five fixture tests named in the node's done-when, plus ruff on the changed paths
reviewed_checklist.goal: Land an accepted run from the landing pass by measuring its suite there, with flakes told apart from regressions
